newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX index slightly up.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in sluggish activity on Friday and brokers said they saw litle chance the mood would change in the near future.
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) main listed market traded 1,425 shares. The most active blue chip was steel maker VSZ, trading 164 stocks. VSZ closed unchanged at 650 crowns.
"The main reason for low liquidity is continuing lack of activity among foreign investors, and I do not expect this to significantly improve in coming days," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
"The reason why foreigners are not active here is that Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of integration to western structures worsened its political instability.
"This seems to be more important than macroeconomic results which are still better than in many other transforming countries," Sykora added.
The top gainer was oil and gas storage company Nafta, which closed up 50 crowns at 1,150, but traded only six shares. Nafta's gains pushed the SAX index up 0.85 to 167.27 points.
Overall volume rose to 831,424 shares, from 213,855 stocks traded on Thursday and the turnover increased to 704.34 million crowns from 67.95 million.
Both volume and turnover were boosted by direct trades.
